paragraphs: BLIP-Diffusion addresses a practical difficulty in personalized image generation: producing new images of a particular subject while following a text prompt. Earlier approaches can require lengthy tuning for each subject and still struggle to preserve its appearance. This paper builds a model that accepts both subject images and text, giving the generator information about what to preserve and what to change.

The central contribution is a pretrained multimodal encoder that supplies a representation of the subject. Its training first follows BLIP-2 to align visual representations with text. A subsequent subject representation learning task teaches the diffusion model to use those representations when creating new renditions. This moves part of the personalization capability into shared pretraining.

The authors report generation for new subjects without subject-specific training, alongside customized fine-tuning with up to a twentyfold speedup over previous methods such as DreamBooth. They also demonstrate combinations with ControlNet and prompt-to-prompt. These results show how the learned representation can support both subject personalization and additional generation or editing controls.
neurips-2023-blip-diffusion-pre-trained-.tldr: BLIP-Diffusion pretrains a subject representation that supports personalized image generation without subject-specific training and faster optional fine-tuning.

paragraphs: This paper studies logical questions about knowledge graphs whose contents include events, activities, and states. Such questions require more than combining relationships between entities. Answers also need to respect constraints on whether situations occur and in what order. For example, an action occurring after a problem is already present is unlikely to explain the problem's onset.

The authors introduce Complex Eventuality Query Answering, or CEQA, to make these implicit requirements part of the task definition. Alongside ordinary first-order logical constraints, CEQA incorporates constraints governing occurrence and temporal order. The proposed benchmark construction uses theorem provers to ensure that the answers satisfy these additional logical requirements, making consistency part of how the task is evaluated.

The paper also introduces Memory-Enhanced Query Encoding, or MEQE, and reports that it significantly improves leading neural query encoders on CEQA. The contribution connects a more demanding definition of a valid answer with a method for improving neural performance on that task. Its stated benefit concerns reasoning over eventualities where relational information and temporal consistency must work together.
neurips-2023-complex-query-answering-on-.tldr: CEQA adds occurrence and temporal constraints to event-graph queries, while MEQE improves neural query encoding for this task.

paragraphs: Fairness evaluations in computer vision often depend on human labels describing perceived attributes, including skin tone. Those labels involve interpretation: lighting affects appearance, and annotators' experiences can affect how they use categories. This paper investigates whether useful agreement is possible while examining systematic differences in how people apply the Monk Skin Tone scale.

The study conducts annotation experiments with a small group of professional photographers and a larger group of trained crowdsourced annotators. It also introduces Monk Skin Tone Examples, a training resource containing 1,515 images and 31 videos across the scale. The resource is intended to help annotators learn how to apply the categories effectively.

The experiments show that annotators can reliably align with an expert's judgments even under challenging environmental conditions. They also provide evidence that annotators in different geographic regions use different mental models, producing systematic regional variation. These findings support using diverse annotators and more judgments per image. Agreement with an expert and variation across groups are both relevant when interpreting labels used for fairness research.
neurips-2023-consensus-and-subjectivity-.tldr: Skin-tone annotators can agree reliably with an expert, yet systematic regional differences support using diverse annotators and repeated judgments.

paragraphs: Models with discrete latent variables represent uncertainty through choices among categories. Training them requires gradients with respect to the probabilities of those choices, but accounting for all possible combinations can be intractable. The common log-derivative trick estimates these gradients from samples and underlies REINFORCE. The paper asks how explicitly using categorical structure can improve that estimation.

The authors introduce the CatLog-Derivative trick, a categorical version of the existing identity. They then derive IndeCateR, an estimator for products of independent categorical distributions. In this setting, the estimator is unbiased, meaning its average estimate matches the target gradient, and has provably lower variance than REINFORCE. The independence condition identifies the setting of this particular theoretical result.

Empirical comparisons show that IndeCateR can be implemented efficiently and produces estimates with significantly lower bias and variance than the compared state-of-the-art methods at the same sample count. The findings distinguish a theoretical guarantee against REINFORCE from broader experimental comparisons. Together, they support exploiting the distribution's discrete structure to obtain more reliable training signals.
neurips-2023-differentiable-sampling-of-.tldr: CatLog yields an unbiased gradient estimator for independent categorical variables with provably lower variance than REINFORCE.

paragraphs: An AI assistant can improve a person's decisions only if the person knows how to use its suggestions. Depending on the situation, useful behavior might involve relying on the system, collaborating with it, or ignoring its advice. This paper proposes learning plain-language rules that teach people how to make those choices for particular kinds of inputs.

The method first discovers local regions of the data, represented as neighborhoods in an embedding space. These regions are selected to correct the human's prior understanding of collaboration. A large language model then describes each region through an iterative, contrastive procedure. This connects the resulting advice to identified data regions rather than leaving it as general guidance about AI use.

The rules are taught through an onboarding stage before people work with the system. User studies involving object detection and question answering show that the method can produce more accurate human-AI teams. The authors also evaluate region discovery and description separately. The stated result supports onboarding as a way to improve collaboration by teaching when different patterns of reliance are appropriate.
neurips-2023-effective-human-ai-teams-vi.tldr: Data-grounded language rules taught during onboarding can help people collaborate with AI more accurately.

paragraphs: A Markov decision process can produce fragile decisions when its model of the environment is uncertain. Robust formulations address this uncertainty, but can be conservative. Distributionally robust formulations additionally use information about how uncertain model parameters are distributed. This paper focuses on making that approach computationally practical when the allowed distributions are described using Wasserstein ambiguity sets.

The main computational target is the distributionally robust Bellman update, an optimization step used in solving the decision problem. The authors exploit its structure to break the associated optimization into smaller subproblems that can be solved efficiently. This decomposition reduces the work required to account for distributional uncertainty during the updates.

For Wasserstein distances built with the L1, L2, or L-infinity norm, the proposed algorithm has complexity that is quasi-linear in both the number of states and the number of actions. Numerical experiments also show better performance than other leading solution methods. The contribution is therefore both a conditional complexity result for these distance choices and empirical evidence that the resulting computations are faster.
neurips-2023-fast-bellman-updates-for-wa.tldr: Structured decomposition makes Wasserstein distributionally robust Bellman updates quasi-linear in states and actions for three specified distance norms.

paragraphs: Auxiliary-task learning trains a model on related tasks to improve performance on a main task. Sometimes those extra tasks make the main task worse, a phenomenon called negative transfer. Existing approaches often attribute this to conflicting gradients and try to coordinate training updates. This paper also examines whether auxiliary-task learning improves generalization on the target task.

The authors investigate negative transfer experimentally from both optimization and generalization perspectives, then introduce ForkMerge. The method periodically creates several branches of the model. It searches over changing task weights using target-task validation error and dynamically merges the branches. The stated purpose of merging is to filter out parameter updates that harm the target task.

Validation performance gives the method a way to judge auxiliary contributions by their usefulness beyond the training objective. Across a series of auxiliary-task benchmarks, ForkMerge outperforms existing methods and mitigates negative transfer. These results support combining branching, task-weight selection, and merging to manage how related tasks influence a shared model, with target-task performance guiding which contributions are useful.
neurips-2023-forkmerge-mitigating-negati.tldr: ForkMerge uses model branches, target validation error, and adaptive merging to reduce harmful transfer from auxiliary tasks.

paragraphs: Graph structure learning adjusts both a graph neural network's parameters and the graph structure used in its computation. Although many methods pursue this idea, inconsistent experimental settings make it difficult to judge progress fairly. GSLB addresses this evaluation problem by bringing multiple methods and datasets into a shared benchmark.

The benchmark includes 20 diverse graph datasets and 16 graph structure learning algorithms. It examines effectiveness, robustness, and complexity, covering tasks that predict properties of individual nodes as well as entire graphs. These dimensions make the comparison broader than a single accuracy ranking: they also examine robust learning and the complexity of the models being evaluated.

The authors provide a library for training, evaluating, and visualizing the methods to support reproducible comparisons. Their experiments demonstrate capabilities of graph structure learning and indicate potential benefits across downstream tasks. The contribution is a common evaluation framework and evidence about behavior in different settings, giving researchers a clearer basis for assessing methods and identifying directions for further work.
neurips-2023-gslb-the-graph-structure-le.tldr: GSLB compares 16 graph structure learning methods across 20 datasets, assessing effectiveness, robustness, and complexity.

paragraphs: This paper asks whether agents adapting their strategies can converge to a Nash equilibrium when each agent uses its own payoff information. The proposed learning dynamics resemble projected gradient ascent but include auxiliary states that can capture dependence on past behavior. They are uncoupled because an agent's updates do not explicitly use other agents' utility functions.

The positive result starts with a particular game having an isolated, completely mixed equilibrium, where every available strategy receives positive probability. For each such game, suitable higher-order gradient dynamics exist that converge locally to that equilibrium. The result also extends to nearby games whose utility functions have been perturbed. Local convergence makes the starting neighborhood relevant.

The negative result reverses the order of selection: for any fixed dynamics in this class, some game with a unique isolated, completely mixed equilibrium defeats convergence. Thus, dynamics suitable for a particular game do not establish a universally successful rule. The authors further show that convergence to mixed equilibria in coordination games requires internal instability in the dynamics, exposing an additional structural tradeoff.
neurips-2023-higher-order-uncoupled-dyna.tldr: Suitable higher-order learning dynamics can converge locally for each qualifying game, but no fixed dynamics work for every such game.

paragraphs: Training can favor particular kinds of neural-network solutions even without an explicit penalty requesting those properties. This tendency is called implicit bias. The paper studies it for gradient descent in two-layer fully connected networks with ReLU or leaky ReLU activations. These nonsmooth activations create a gap between existing understanding of gradient descent and results about continuous-time gradient flow.

The theoretical analysis assumes that the training examples are nearly orthogonal. Under this condition, gradient descent produces leaky ReLU networks whose stable rank converges to one. For ReLU networks, the stable rank remains bounded above by a constant. Stable rank describes effective dimensionality, so these results characterize a tendency toward low-dimensional learned structure, with different conclusions for the two activation functions.

The authors also show that all training examples approach the same normalized margin asymptotically. This describes a further regularity in the eventual solution beyond its rank. Experiments on synthetic and real data support the theoretical findings. The work clarifies what discrete gradient-descent training favors in this specified setting, rather than treating continuous-time analysis as sufficient.
neurips-2023-implicit-bias-of-gradient-d.tldr: On nearly orthogonal data, gradient descent favors bounded stable rank and asymptotically equal normalized margins in two-layer ReLU-family networks.

paragraphs: This paper demonstrates reinforcement learning through changes to a language model's prompt. Its goal is to implement policy iteration, repeatedly updating how the system chooses actions as it gains experience. The motivation is to avoid collecting expert demonstrations or adapting the model with gradient-based training, both of which introduce substantial work before or during task adaptation.

The method interacts with a reinforcement-learning environment through trial and error. It uses that experience to iteratively revise the prompt from which its policy is derived. Learning therefore occurs through the changing context supplied to the model, allowing the approach to use in-context learning without updating model parameters for the task.

The authors demonstrate the method with Codex, which they describe as having no prior knowledge of the evaluated domains. This choice is intended to separate the demonstrated learning from domain knowledge already stored in the model's weights. The result establishes a way for a language model to implement policy iteration without expert demonstrations or gradients, showing that the prompt itself can carry task adaptation.
neurips-2023-large-language-models-can-i.tldr: A language model can implement policy iteration by updating its prompt through trial-and-error interaction, without expert demonstrations or gradient updates.

paragraphs: Computational lithography uses algorithms to support the optical patterning step in semiconductor manufacturing. Simulating that process and optimizing masks can be expensive, limiting the practical use of inverse lithography technology. Machine-learning approaches have shown promise for reducing this burden, but the paper identifies a shortage of data for thorough training and comprehensive evaluation.

LithoBench provides more than 120,000 circuit-layout tiles for two tasks: lithography simulation and mask optimization. The tiles come from real circuit designs or are synthesized using the layout topologies of established inverse-lithography test cases. Reference outputs are generated using an academic lithography model and an advanced inverse-lithography method, supplying targets for the benchmark's learning tasks.

The accompanying framework supports the design and evaluation of deep neural networks, and the authors use it to benchmark leading models on both tasks. The contribution is a shared dataset and evaluation framework for studying AI-assisted computational lithography. It gives researchers a common basis for investigating whether learned simulation and optimization methods can reduce the computational obstacles motivating the work.
neurips-2023-lithobench-benchmarking-ai-.tldr: LithoBench supplies over 120,000 circuit-layout tiles and a framework for evaluating learned lithography simulation and mask optimization.

paragraphs: Visual question answering requires a model to connect an image with a question and produce an answer. Assessing complex logical reasoning within that process is difficult without questions whose requirements and correct answers are formally defined. This paper introduces LoRA, a dataset designed to evaluate such reasoning systematically using a food-and-kitchen knowledge base.

The authors build programs that automatically generate 200,000 diverse reasoning questions, accompanied by realistic kitchen scenes and ground-truth answers. The questions use SROIQ Description Logic, providing a formal basis for the reasoning they demand. This design ties the evaluation to explicit logical questions instead of relying solely on broadly framed image understanding tasks.

The evaluation includes fine-tuning transformer-based visual-question-answering models and testing leading large vision-and-language models without task-specific examples. The results indicate that LoRA poses a distinctive logical reasoning challenge. Its contribution is an evaluation resource aimed at measuring complex formal reasoning more comprehensively, with the longer-term objective of improving those capabilities in models that combine visual and linguistic information.
neurips-2023-lora-a-logical-reasoning-au.tldr: LoRA pairs kitchen scenes with 200,000 formally generated questions to test complex logical reasoning in visual question answering.

paragraphs: The paper studies parameter estimation when observations come from a mixture of a known background density and a second density with unknown parameters. The mixture weight determines the proportion contributed by the second component. The authors analyze maximum likelihood estimation, which selects parameters that make the observed data most probable under this model.

Two features complicate the analysis. The background and the second density can interact in ways that make their contributions difficult to distinguish. Also, the mixture weight can approach either endpoint of its allowed range as the sample size grows. In particular, when the second component's proportion shrinks toward zero, increasing the dataset size changes both the amount and the composition of available evidence.

To describe the first issue, the authors introduce a distinguishability condition based on linear independence between the two functions. They then characterize convergence rates in relation to this condition and the speed at which the mixture weight vanishes. The result connects estimation accuracy to both component separability and the shrinking proportion of observations attributable to the unknown component.
neurips-2023-minimax-optimal-rate-for-pa.tldr: The paper characterizes maximum-likelihood convergence rates through component distinguishability and how quickly an unknown mixture component's proportion vanishes.

paragraphs: Structured prediction produces outputs whose parts depend on one another, as in image segmentation or scene graphs. Treating those parts as independent misses this internal structure, while the number of possible complete outputs can grow exponentially. This paper develops a PAC-Bayesian risk bound to reason about generalization in that setting.

The bound's generalization rate depends on both the number of structured examples and their size. Its key assumption concerns how the data are generated: a Knothe-Rosenblatt rearrangement transforms a factorizing reference measure into the data distribution. In plain terms, the analysis starts from an independent reference distribution and uses a specified transformation to represent the dependencies in the observed outputs.

This construction allows the authors to summarize relationships among output variables in a Wasserstein dependency matrix. That representation connects the assumed generative process to a guarantee for a discriminative prediction task. The paper presents this as a preliminary step toward using powerful generative models to certify generalization, with the stated generation assumption central to the proposed bound.
neurips-2023-on-certified-generalization.tldr: A new structured-prediction generalization bound accounts for example size under a specified generative assumption that represents output dependencies.

paragraphs: Matrix completion predicts missing entries in a low-rank table from the entries that have been observed, potentially with noise. Uneven observation patterns can make prediction quality vary sharply across the table. In movie ratings, for example, users may mainly rate familiar genres or films from their own country, leaving other parts of the matrix poorly supported.

The paper changes the objective to partial matrix completion: accurately fill a substantial subset of entries with high confidence. Its algorithm handles an unknown sampling distribution even when that distribution has arbitrarily complex structure. The stated guarantees combine high accuracy for every completed entry with sufficient coverage, addressing both reliability and how much of the matrix gets completed.

The authors also formulate an online version and provide an efficient algorithm based on iterative gradient updates with low regret. A preliminary empirical evaluation accompanies the methods. The contribution makes the choice of which entries to complete part of the problem itself, explicitly connecting the amount of completion to confidence in the resulting predictions.
neurips-2023-partial-matrix-completion-0.tldr: Partial matrix completion seeks a substantial, reliably predicted subset of missing entries despite unknown and complex sampling patterns.

paragraphs: A contextual bandit chooses an action using information about the current situation and learns from the resulting feedback. The information revealed by a choice can vary: it may concern only that action or provide information about others as well. This paper studies how to use such feedback patterns to make learning more statistically efficient.

Feedback graphs describe the available information and cover settings between ordinary bandit feedback and full information. The authors propose an approach that reduces contextual-bandit learning with these graphs to regression. This reduction gives the decision problem a computational form built around predictive estimation, while retaining an explicit role for which feedback is available.

The paper analyzes the resulting algorithms and shows that they achieve established minimax rates, meaning their worst-case statistical performance matches the relevant known rates. It also describes the algorithms as computationally practical. The contribution connects these two requirements: using richer feedback to reduce the statistical difficulty of learning, while supplying a regression-based approach intended to make those benefits usable in applications.
neurips-2023-practical-contextual-bandit.tldr: A regression-based approach makes contextual bandits with feedback graphs computationally practical while achieving established minimax rates.

paragraphs: A contextual-bandit experiment can pursue two different goals: make good decisions throughout the experiment or learn a strong policy to use afterward. Cumulative regret measures the first concern, while simple regret measures the quality of the final policy. This paper introduces efficient algorithms with a tuning parameter controlling how much emphasis each goal receives.

The algorithms use conformal arm sets, which assign candidate actions to each context. Across the context distribution, these sets contain the context-specific best action with a specified probability. This coverage property supports algorithms that accommodate any function class, tolerate model misspecification, and extend to continuous action spaces. The guarantee concerns coverage across contexts rather than certainty for every individual context.

The authors establish near-optimal minimax cumulative-regret guarantees and state-of-the-art simple-regret guarantees. They also prove a boundary: no algorithm can combine instance-dependent simple-regret guarantees with minimax-optimal cumulative-regret guarantees. The work therefore provides a way to tune the two objectives while identifying a theoretical restriction on how strong both types of guarantee can be simultaneously.
neurips-2023-proportional-response-conte.tldr: Conformal arm sets support contextual-bandit algorithms that trade off final-policy quality against performance during learning, with guarantees and an impossibility result.

paragraphs: Detecting defects in precision manufacturing requires detailed representations of object shape. This paper addresses the shortage of datasets and systematic evaluation for high-precision anomaly detection in point clouds, where objects are represented by collections of three-dimensional points. It introduces Real3D-AD as both a dataset and a basis for benchmarking methods.

The dataset contains 1,254 high-resolution items, with individual items ranging from forty thousand to millions of points. The authors report resolution of 0.0010–0.0015 millimeters, full 360-degree coverage, and perfect prototypes as advantages over existing datasets. These properties make fine geometric detail and comprehensive object coverage central to the evaluation setting.

The accompanying benchmark identifies a gap in baseline methods suited to this task. The authors respond with Reg3D-AD, a registration-based detector that incorporates a feature memory bank preserving both local and global representations. Extensive experiments on Real3D-AD support its effectiveness. The released dataset, benchmark code, and method together provide resources for comparing approaches under the paper's high-precision industrial detection setting.
neurips-2023-real3d-ad-a-dataset-of-poin.tldr: Real3D-AD provides high-resolution industrial point clouds, a benchmark, and a registration-based method for detecting geometric anomalies.

paragraphs: Adversarial robustness distillation transfers resistance to adversarial inputs from a large teacher model to a smaller student. Overall robustness can conceal uneven protection: some data classes may remain much easier to attack than others. This paper examines that imbalance, using robust fairness to describe how robustness is distributed across classes.

The authors find that students inherit only part of their teachers' robust fairness. Experiments across model capacities suggest that the teacher-student capacity gap and equal treatment of classes during distillation may contribute. Their proposed Fair-ARD framework increases the weights of difficult classes, using a geometrically motivated measure of class difficulty to determine those weights.

Experiments show better robust fairness than both leading distillation methods and existing robust-fairness algorithms, alongside slight improvements in overall robustness. With ResNet18 on CIFAR10 under AutoAttack, reported worst-class robustness improvements are at most 12.3% and 5.3% against those respective groups. These findings support class-sensitive distillation as a way to improve protection for vulnerable classes when transferring robustness into smaller models.
neurips-2023-revisiting-adversarial-robu.tldr: Fair-ARD emphasizes difficult classes during robustness distillation, improving worst-class protection and slightly improving overall robustness in experiments.

paragraphs: Language models usually generate tokens sequentially, making decoding slow. Speculative decoding lets a smaller model propose tokens that a larger model scores in parallel, with an acceptance rule preserving the larger model's output distribution. SpecTr develops this idea through optimal transport, framing draft selection as a problem with a membership cost.

This formulation permits multiple candidates at each token position and improves the optimal membership cost. An exact transport plan can be found by linear programming, but the best-known runtime is exponential in the candidate count. The authors instead provide a valid selection algorithm whose acceptance probability is within a multiplicative factor of one minus one over e of optimal, with runtime almost linear in the token-domain size.

SpecTr uses this selection rule to accelerate sampling while preserving the target output distribution. Experiments report a 2.13-fold wall-clock speedup and a further 1.37-fold improvement over speculative decoding on standard benchmarks. The theoretical approximation concerns acceptance efficiency; the algorithm still preserves the larger model's sampling distribution, which underpins the stated absence of output-quality degradation.
neurips-2023-spectr-fast-speculative-dec.tldr: SpecTr uses optimal-transport-based selection among draft candidates to accelerate decoding while preserving the large model's output distribution.

paragraphs: Personalized image generators can learn a subject from a few examples, but training a separate expert for every subject is expensive. SuTI aims to make a new subject usable immediately through in-context examples. Given a few demonstrations, it generates new renditions in different scenes without performing subject-specific optimization.

The method obtains this ability through apprenticeship learning. The authors mine millions of image clusters from the Internet, each organized around a visual subject, and use them to train many subject-specific experts. A single apprentice model then learns to imitate those experts from the data they generate. The work of learning individual experts thus supplies training experience for a reusable generator.

The authors report customized image generation twenty times faster than optimization-based state-of-the-art methods. Human evaluations on DreamBench and DreamBench-v2 also show significant improvements over the compared models, including DreamBooth. These findings support learning a shared model from many specialists as a way to provide subject customization at use time through examples, while retaining the benefits of extensive expert-based training beforehand.
neurips-2023-subject-driven-text-to-imag.tldr: SuTI learns from many subject-specific experts to personalize image generation from examples without optimizing a new model for each subject.

paragraphs: Long-range probabilistic forecasting must represent possible future sequences while maintaining relationships across time. Autoregressive models build sequences through conditional predictions, but long chains can accumulate errors and make distant dependencies difficult to capture. SutraNets changes how a long sequence is organized to reduce these difficulties.

The method treats one high-frequency series as several lower-frequency sub-series and forecasts them as a multivariate problem. Autoregression proceeds both across time and between sub-series, maintaining coherence when their outputs are interpreted as the original series. Because each sub-series requires fewer generation steps, this organization reduces error accumulation and shortens the paths over which distant information must travel.

The authors report significantly better forecasting accuracy than competitive alternatives on six real-world datasets. Improvements also hold in experiments that vary the number of sub-series and increase the depth and width of the underlying sequence models. The findings support reorganizing the forecasting dependency structure as a useful component of long-sequence modeling, alongside choices about the capacity of the neural network itself.
neurips-2023-sutranets-sub-series-autore.tldr: SutraNets forecasts linked lower-frequency sub-series to reduce long autoregressive chains, improving accuracy on six real-world datasets.

paragraphs: Understanding a hand interaction involves identifying the hand, the objects involved, and the kind of contact taking place. This paper introduces a model that produces a richer description of those interactions in two-dimensional images. The aim is to give AI systems more of the information people obtain by watching how others use their hands.

The outputs include bounding boxes and segmentation regions for hands, objects in contact with them, and second objects touched by tools. The model also predicts contact and grasp types. Including second objects extends the description beyond the hand's immediate contact, representing interactions in which a tool connects the hand to another object.

The work is supported by annotations spanning four datasets: 257,000 images, 401,000 hands, 288,000 objects, and 19,000 second objects. The authors report that the method provides rich information, performs well, and generalizes well. Its contribution combines a broader interaction description with annotation at substantial scale, allowing multiple aspects of hand-object interaction to be addressed together.
neurips-2023-towards-a-richer-2d-underst.tldr: A large-scale hand-understanding system predicts hands, contacted objects, tool-mediated objects, and contact and grasp types from images.

paragraphs: Regression predicts numerical values, and unevenly distributed target values can cause problems for both accuracy and uncertainty estimates. Variational imbalanced regression, or VIR, addresses these together through a probabilistic deep-learning model. Its design allows information from examples with similar target values to influence how an example is represented.

Specifically, VIR uses nearby regression labels when computing the probability distribution of a latent representation. This differs from treating each representation as unaffected by other examples. It also predicts normal-inverse-gamma distributions rather than only individual numerical estimates. The model adjusts the associated conjugate distributions to reweight imbalanced data probabilistically, linking its treatment of imbalance with its uncertainty output.

Experiments on several real-world datasets show that VIR can outperform leading imbalanced-regression models in both predictive accuracy and uncertainty estimation. The findings support combining information sharing among similar labels with distribution-valued predictions. In this approach, uncertainty estimation is produced within the regression model itself, and the mechanism for addressing label imbalance is incorporated into the same probabilistic formulation.
neurips-2023-variational-imbalanced-regr.tldr: VIR combines information from similar labels with probabilistic reweighting to improve regression accuracy and uncertainty estimation under label imbalance.
